title: The Electroweak Structure of the E6 in the Selection–Stitch Model: Chirality, the Weak Mixing Angle, and the Charge the Photon Sees
content: In the Selection–Stitch Model the vacuum is a face-centered-cubic lattice, and labeling each matter weight by the up or down orientation of its tetrahedral void builds the root system of \( E_6 \). We work out the electroweak structure it allows. With the electric charge fixed by earlier work, a weak \( \mathfrak{su}(2) \) generated by a root can sit in only two places, which the orientation flip exchanges. The left placement gives the hypercharges of one Standard Model generation plus the usual \( E_6 \) extra states, with no free parameter. The choice between the placements is a single bit that no flip-symmetric quantity can set. The hypercharge normalization is \( 5/3 \), and the weak mixing angle is \( 3/8 \) when the two exchanged couplings are equal, as the static crystal's inversion symmetry suggests. Two neutral singlets break trinification to the Standard Model group, and a neutral doublet member then leaves color and electromagnetism. A hop of a defect applies the flip, and the electric charge is the only unbroken charge that every hop conserves. This is the condition for minimal coupling to the lattice photon of earlier work. One-loop running places the matching scale near \( 10^{13}~GeV \). A public script checks every computed claim.
